# A body edit's rerun leaves the first run's red on the PR head

## Context

Operator, 2026-10-23: the second half of the merged-PRs-read-red item (#20061 / PR #20062 took the first). After the controller's post-merge runs leave the merged heads, 7 of the 30 most recently merged PRs still roll up `FAILURE`, from 8 red contexts of one class: a check that ran twice on the same head and whose first run's conclusion stayed.

| red context | count | PRs |
|---|---|---|
| `File Size Guard / check-size` `CANCELLED`, a later run of the same name `SUCCESS` on the same head | 6 | #20053, #20037, #20032, #20019, #19998 |
| `PR Baseline / baseline / PR body` `FAILURE`, a later run `SUCCESS` on the same head | 2 | #20000, #19997 |

GitHub's rollup (the field the PR list icon renders, as "59/60 checks passing" with a red mark) counts every check run on the SHA, not the latest per name: #20032 carries two cancelled `check-size` runs (07:17Z, 07:20Z) and three green ones (07:22Z, 07:36Z, 08:08Z) and rolls up `FAILURE`. The merge gate reads the latest run per required context, which is why these PRs merged clean while reading red.

Live specimen and mechanism proof, 14:0xZ: PR #20063 (head a949c64086) opened at 14:00Z; `check-size` run 39965984915 (created 14:00:42Z) was cancelled when the body-edit run 39966042076 arrived at 14:01:05Z under the workflow's `cancel-in-progress: true` group; the edit run passed; rollup `FAILURE`. `gh run rerun 39965984915` at 14:11:51Z → attempt 2 `success` at 14:12:39Z → rollup `SUCCESS` (63 green, 1 skipped), the cancelled entry gone: a re-run replaces the conclusion in place.

Prior sightings on the record: Mnemosyne read the cancelled `check-size` as a superseded duplicate on PR #19352 (10-01) and PR #19587 (10-11) and adopted a workaround (edit the body before the push or after green); Grace (08-17) found that a re-run replays the frozen event payload, so a body gate reading `github.event.pull_request.body` can never pass on re-run, which is why the baseline's `pr-body` job now fetches the body live (`reusable-pr-baseline.yml` v0.1.55:468–489), as does `file-size-guard.yml:43–55`. That property is what the fix below depends on.

Live latest-open sweep: the newest 20 open issues at 14:13Z, no equivalent (#20061 is the controller half). A2A claims in the last hour: none on this surface. Memory Core rationale sweep: the three sightings above, no prior fix. Own open assignments: #20061 (the sibling), none else on this surface.

## The Problem

Two workflows re-run on an unchanged head when the PR body changes (`pull_request: edited`), by design: both read the body (the size ratchet's justification marker, the PR-body anchors). Each `edited` event starts a new workflow run, a new check suite with check runs of the same names, and the earlier suite's conclusions stay on the SHA:

1. **`File Size Guard`** cancels the in-progress run of the same ref when the edit arrives (`concurrency.group: file-size-guard-${ref}`, `cancel-in-progress: true`, `file-size-guard.yml:21-23`). The cancelled run is a red check run on the head for good; agents edit the body right after opening a PR, so the cancellation is routine (6 of 30 PRs).
2. **`PR Baseline / PR body`** fails on a body that misses an anchor and passes once the author edits it, the designed fail-fix-pass flow. The first run's `FAILURE` stays beside the later `SUCCESS` (2 of 30). `File Size Guard`'s own ratchet has the same designed flow (fail, add the justification, pass): 0 of 30 today, structural all the same.

Neither workflow can fix this from inside a run: check runs cannot be deleted, and GitHub offers no latest-per-name rollup. What does work is re-running the first run after the head has a green run of the same workflow: re-runs replace the conclusion in place (the specimen above), and both jobs read the live PR, so the re-run judges the corrected body, not the frozen payload.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/file-size-guard.yml:7-10` triggers on `opened, edited, synchronize, ready_for_review` with a paths filter; `:21-23` the concurrency group with cancellation; `:43-55` fetches the live body for `--pr-body-file`. The repo-wide `run_attempt == '1' && github.ref || github.run_id` idiom (#15593) governs workflows that cancel; a workflow with no `concurrency` block is outside its scope by construction.
- `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml:55-57` triggers on the same four events and calls `neomjs/neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml@v0.1.55`; it has no concurrency block, so its runs never cancel each other (0 cancellations in the data). Its ten jobs are required contexts in the `dev` ruleset (`gh api repos/neomjs/neo/rules/branches/dev`); the file's header still says `dev` carries no `required_status_checks` rule, a comment drift noted as a defect-note, not touched here.
- `reusable-pr-baseline.yml` v0.1.55 `pr-body` (`:438-520`) fetches the body with `pulls.get` and runs `neo-agent-skills-pr-body`; no checkout.
- GitHub: `workflow_run` runs execute in the base repository from the default branch's workflow file, with a token that may hold `actions: write`, and anchor their own check runs on the default-branch commit they ran from (`github.sha`), while the payload carries the triggering run's `head_sha`, `workflow_id` and `run_number`; `actions.listWorkflowRuns` filters by `workflow_id` + `head_sha`; `actions.reRunWorkflow` / `reRunWorkflowFailedJobs` start a new attempt whose job conclusions replace the previous attempt's in the suite (the specimen); re-runs keep the original run's actor, SHA and ref.
- The durable home for the repair is the Skills corpus' reusable baseline, which every consumer repository calls; a consumer cannot change it from here and the tag pin moves by release. The repository-local shape below is the one that ships in the v13.3.1 window; it retires when the upstream shape lands (sunset condition in Out of Scope).

Design authority: #15593's rerun-isolation contract is the idiom for workflows that cancel; removing File Size Guard's cancellation takes it out of that contract's scope rather than bending it. The body-edit trigger stays load-bearing (`pr-baseline.yml:15-20`); nothing here changes what is linted or when.

## The Fix

1. **`file-size-guard.yml`: delete the `concurrency` block** (3 lines). Two runs on the same head both complete; a `synchronize` run's predecessor finishes on the old SHA, invisible on the new head. Cost: one redundant ~40 s job per rapid body edit.
2. **New `.github/workflows/same-head-check-repair.yml`**: `on: workflow_run: workflows: [PR Baseline, File Size Guard], types: [completed]`, `permissions: actions: write`, one `github-script` job that, when the completed run is `success` from a `pull_request` event on an open PR, lists that workflow's runs on the same `head_sha` and re-runs each completed run whose conclusion is `failure`, `cancelled` or `timed_out`, whose `run_attempt` is 1 and whose per-workflow `run_number` is lower than the witness's (failed jobs only for `failure`, all jobs for `cancelled` / `timed_out`); API errors become `core.warning`, never a failed job, because the job's own check run sits on the `dev` commit the event ran from and a red there is a red on `dev`. The loop terminates: a repaired run completes green and lists nothing to repair, the attempt bound stops a run that fails twice, and the run-number bound keeps an old green that finishes late from spending a newer red run's retry before the author's fix has run (Euclid's RA-1 on PR #20066).
3. Nothing else: PR Baseline's caller, the reusable workflow, the ruleset and both lint scripts are untouched.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `File Size Guard` runs on one head | the workflow's trigger set (unchanged) | every run completes; none cancels a sibling on the same ref | none needed | the file's trigger comment | AC-1 |
| `Same-Head Check Repair` (new) | `workflow_run` of the two body-reading workflows | after a green run on a head, red runs of the same workflow on that head with a lower run number are re-run once | the repair job never fails; an API refusal is a warning and the stale red stays, as today | workflow header | AC-2, AC-3 |
| required contexts `baseline / *` | `dev` ruleset | unchanged (the latest run per name already governs the gate) | — | — | the ruleset read |

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 **No same-head cancellation:** `file-size-guard.yml` has no `concurrency` key; on this ticket's PR, a body edit during an in-flight `check-size` run leaves two `check-size` `SUCCESS` entries and no `CANCELLED` entry in the head's rollup (the PR touches the guard's own file, so the guard runs).
- [ ] AC-2 **Repair, evaluated:** the committed repair script, run against a mocked `actions` API with runs `[A: failure attempt 1, B: the completed success (self), C: cancelled attempt 2, D: in_progress, N: a newer failure attempt 1]`, re-runs exactly A (failed jobs) and nothing else; with C at attempt 1 it re-runs A and C (C all jobs); an older green completing after the newer failure N re-runs nothing, and a later green re-runs N once; with the PR closed, or the triggering run not `success`, or its event not `pull_request`, it re-runs nothing. Output in the PR body.
- [ ] AC-3 **Never red itself:** the same harness with every `actions` call throwing ends with warnings and no `setFailed`.
- [ ] AC-4 **Post-merge only:** for the first PR after this lands whose `PR body` job fails and then passes on a body edit, the head's rollup shows the first run at attempt 2 `success` within minutes of the green run and no stale `FAILURE`; receipt on this ticket.

## Out of Scope

- The upstream home: a `neomjs/neo-agent-skills` ticket to fold the repair into `reusable-pr-baseline.yml` (serving every consumer), filed as the follow-up; when it ships and the pin moves, `same-head-check-repair.yml` loses its `PR Baseline` entry, and retires once File Size Guard moves there too.
- Retroactive repair of the 7 merged PRs: a re-run of a merged PR's `check-size` checks out a merge ref that no longer exists; the baseline's `pr-body` has no checkout and would repair; the operator's call whether old history is worth touching.
- `pr-baseline.yml`'s header drift (says no required contexts; the ruleset requires all ten): defect-note.
- The `dev` commit list's red (test runs cancelled by the next merge): a runner-budget decision.
- Two green witnesses completing within the same seconds may both request the same re-run; GitHub refuses the second (the run is already in progress) and the refusal is a warning. Not exercised against GitHub; the first week's `Same-Head Check Repair` run logs show it if it happens.

## Avoided Traps

- **`cancel-in-progress: false` for File Size Guard:** keeps one running and one pending job and cancels a third arrival's predecessor; three events within a run's 40 s still leave a cancelled entry.
- **Re-running on `edited` instead of a fresh run:** the fresh run is the event's own evidence; the repair re-runs the old run only after a green one exists, so a re-run can never outrank a green with a red (Grace's 08-17 trap, in reverse).
- **Completion order as "earlier":** a success that completes later is not a later success; the witness relation is the per-workflow run number (RA-1).
- **Status-context verdicts for the lints:** latest-write-wins would need the required contexts rebound in the ruleset (#17171's domain) and a change to the reusable workflow.
- **Dropping `edited`:** the body gates stop re-judging corrected bodies (`pr-baseline.yml:15-20`).
